scores.evidence: Phase 1: Contracts and the PAN boundary ... Depends on: V0. Phase 3 "Depends on: V1, V3 (build), V4."
scores.rationale: Phases run substrate (skeleton, PAN boundary, schema) to defenses, features, model, live, feedback, with explicit dependency table and gates proving each before the next.

scores.evidence: a $1 card-not-present authorization on an issuer test card in the production test BIN range ... tokenizes the PAN ... decision log to S3
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a genuine thin end-to-end production path with deploy, rollback, trace and case creation before any features.

scores.evidence: Default | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition ... V2 fails, or the QSA rejects the scope reduction: the whole pipeline enters PCI scope
scores.rationale: Irreversible R3 decisions are tabulated with default, assumption, validation and flip conditions, plus labeled assumptions and missing inputs.

scores.evidence: Exposure ladder ... internal cards → 1% of one low-risk BIN segment → 5% → 25% → 100% of that segment
scores.rationale: Within phases, widest-impact items (PAN boundary, schema, timeout/kill switch/signed config) precede leaf work, and exposure ordering is deliberate, though not explicitly described as blast-radius ordering everywhere.

scores.evidence: Test BINs only; tokenize in the adapter; mTLS; secrets in KMS/Vault
scores.rationale: The cross-cutting table gives concrete security content for every phase 0–6.

scores.evidence: OTel trace across all tiers; latency/timeout/lag alerts
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and every later phase.

scores.evidence: Terraform, pinned images, GitOps, config in git
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is addressed in every phase from Terraform and pinned images through snapshot IDs, registry lineage and seeded retraining.

scores.evidence: 80 ms timeout; output ignored; flag and Argo rollback
scores.rationale: Resilience content appears in every phase, from the timeout and rollback in Phase 0 through replication, breaker and retrain-failure handling.

scores.evidence: 1. Guardrail defense ... Phase 2; 3. Human-in-the-loop ... Phases 2, 4, 5; 4. Retrieval Phase 3; 5. Model access Phase 4; 9. Feedback Phase 6
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and HITL precede retrieval, model access, memory, orchestration and feedback in order, with routing explicitly deferred; the plan is classical ML, so the layers are adapted sensibly.

scores.evidence: Decommissioning the existing engine. Pull forward when the new model has run at 100% for 2 full label cycles
scores.rationale: Each deferred item has a concrete pull-forward condition.

note: Exceptionally thorough plan that meets every rubric dimension with concrete content; the only minor gap is that blast-radius ordering is implicit rather than named.
